Air Quality - Neighborhood Areas
Most of the climate and air quality elements previously identified and discussed in the city-wide context are equally applicable to the local neighborhoods in the Alviso, Alum Rock, Central and Willow Glen Plannings Areas. Air quality problems in these localities are the result of area-wide physiography and inversion conditions, low winds, intense solar radiation and sizeable pollutant emission for both local and regional sources.
Motor vehicles account for the majority of carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen oxide (NO<sub>X</sub>) and hydrocarbon (HC) regional emissions: 85%, 55%, and 44% respectively. Motor vehicles also contribute 25% of the particulates and 8% of the sulfur dioxide emissions (SO<sub>2</sub>).
Although all the neighborhoods targeted for CDBG funding are essentially residential in character, most experience significant amounts of vehicular traffic through or very near. The Alviso CNRA is singularly free from heavy traffic volumes.
Alma CNRA:
Bounded on the north by West Alma Avenue, a major east-west corridor and by Monterey Highway, Route 84, a major north-south thoroughfare.
Alviso CNRA:
Alviso's bayside location gives it a favorable combination of climatic conditions, such as slightly cooler afternoon temperatures, stronger than average on-shore winds which are unimpeded by dense urbanization. These positive conditions coupled with Alviso's very low vehicular traffic give Alviso the cleanest air of all of San Jose's planning areas.
Campus CNRA:
Bordered on the north by Santa Clara Street, a major arterial and on the south by San Fernando, a collector, and on the west by Fourth Street, another collector. The Campus CNRA borders the heart of downtown San Jose, a significant source of vehicular-generated pollutants.*
Gardner CNRA:
Bisected by Bird Avenue, a major collector and the Southern Pacific Railroad mainline. Bounded on the south by Willow Street, another major collector and on the north by Route 280. (The proposed extension of the Guadalupe Expressway, Route 87, is planned at the easterly border of Gardner CNRA.
Mayfair CNRA:
Surrounded on the south and east by Route 680; bordered on the north by Alum Rock Avenue, a major arterial and on the west by a major collector, King Road, bisected by another major collector, San Antonio Street.
* 
Detailed studies show that heavy traffic and street canyon vortex phenonenma in central San Jose exert a profound influence on the area's micrometerology. Johnson, et al, 1973: Ott, et al, 1973.
